item.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM is now the GenAI Security Project and promoted to OWASP Flagship status
item.description:
Author: OWASPGenAIProject Editor
Date: (Publication date unknown)
Tags: ["Cybersecurity", "Generative AI", "Open Source", "Risk Management", "Artificial Intelligence"]
Summary:
  • OWASP renamed its LLM project to the GenAI Security Project.
  • The initiative has been promoted to prestigious OWASP Flagship status.
  • This change reflects an expanded focus beyond simple vulnerability lists.
  • New resources now cover governance, deepfakes, and agentic AI threats.
  • Over 600 experts currently contribute to these open-source security tools.
  • The project aims to ensure secure deployment of generative AI systems.

item.title: Project Silica’s advances in glass storage technology

  • The technology now works with affordable borosilicate glass.
  • New techniques allow for faster parallel data writing.
  • Simplified readers and single laser pulses reduce overall costs.
  • This innovation offers a durable alternative to degrading magnetic media.

item.title: Media Authenticity Methods in Practice: Capabilities, Limitations, and Directions
item.description:

Date: February 19, 2026
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Digital Provenance", "Media Integrity", "Cybersecurity", "Data Privacy"]
Summary:
  • AI makes it harder to distinguish real media from synthetic content.
  • Microsoft evaluated technologies that verify the source and history of digital media.
  • These methods include watermarks, fingerprinting, and C2PA provenance standards.
  • New legislation and adversarial attacks are driving the need for better authentication.
  • The report outlines practical steps to strengthen media integrity and public trust.
  • Consistent implementation across the digital ecosystem remains essential for success.

item.title: CORPGEN advances AI agents for real work
item.description:
Author: Abubakarr Jaye, Nigel Boachie Kumankumah, Chidera Biringa, Anjel Patel, Dayquan Julienne, Tianwei Chen, Sulaiman Vesal
Date: February 26, 2026
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Productivity Software", "Machine Learning", "Enterprise Technology"]
Summary:
  • Microsoft Research introduced CORPGEN to improve AI workplace productivity.
  • Current AI agents struggle with managing multiple interdependent tasks simultaneously.
  • Performance often drops significantly when agents face heavy multi-task loads.
  • CORPGEN uses hierarchical planning and memory isolation to solve these issues.
  • This modular system delivers much higher completion rates than standard baselines.
  • The architecture works across different underlying AI models to enhance performance.

Summary:
  • Microsoft released Phi-4-reasoning-vision-15B as an open-weight model.
  • This 15 billion parameter model handles diverse vision-language tasks.
  • It excels at math, science, and user-interface understanding.
  • The model balances high reasoning power with computational efficiency.

item.title: From raw interaction to reusable knowledge: Rethinking memory for AI agents
item.description:
Author: Ke Yang, Michel Galley, Chenglong Wang, Jianfeng Gao, Jiawei Han, ChengXiang Zhai
Date: March 10, 2026
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Machine Learning", "Knowledge Management", "AI Agents"]
Summary:
  • Current AI agents struggle to manage long interaction histories.
  • Raw memory retrieval often overwhelms agents with irrelevant data.
  • Researchers developed PlugMem to transform history into structured knowledge.
  • This system converts interactions into compact facts and reusable skills.
  • A structured memory graph improves retrieval speed and precision.
  • PlugMem enhances agent performance while using fewer memory tokens.
